summary: Bye in ASL is a wave, often with the fingers folding down toward the palm. It's the same sign for goodbye and see you.
movement: Fingers fold down and open, or a side-to-side wave
steps: Raise an open hand at shoulder height, palm facing the person.
Fold your fingers down toward the palm and open them again, once or twice.
Keep eye contact until you turn away. Breaking eye contact is how you actually end a signed conversation.
note: Deaf goodbyes are famously long. Expect to sign BYE, get pulled into one more conversation, and sign it again ten minutes later. That's normal and it's a sign that people enjoy talking to you.
mistakes: Looking away before you finish signing. In ASL, breaking eye contact is a stronger signal than the sign itself.

faq.q: How do I say 'see you later' instead of just bye?
faq.a: Use the phrase SEE-YOU-LATER: the SEE sign (a V handshape at the eyes) moving forward, then LATER. It's on its own page.
